title: OpenAI withdraws three preprints a day after releasing 722 manuscripts on unsolved math problems
key_facts: On 6 Oct 2026 OpenAI published 722 preprints in a GitHub repository about purported progress on 372 maths problems.
On 7 Oct OpenAI withdrew three manuscripts because of a sign error that invalidated one argument and the construction used by two dependent papers.
OpenAI also revised 14 other manuscripts with proof repairs and corrections.
Cornell mathematician Alex Townsend suspects more errors will be found and said the Lean-verified results should have been announced first.
An OpenAI spokesperson said the errors were found in an audit, and that about 50% of results were released unconfirmed on the advice of the AGMAI group.
MIT's Andrew Sutherland called the quick withdrawal "the responsible thing to do" but said it will take much more to regain trust.
The Association for Human Mathematics criticised the release in a statement on 7 Oct.
quote_evidence: Less than 24 hours after OpenAI posted over 700 preprints describing major math results by an internal AI model, the company has withdrawn three of the manuscripts for errors.
The error invalidated an argument in one manuscript and the construction used by two dependent papers, according to the announcement.
why_it_matters_hint: The first errors in a huge AI-written maths release have appeared within a day, and a mathematician expects more.
notes: Follow-up of X30 (7 Oct 2026). Same cluster as C04-01, C04-07, C04-17.
